article_title: Promoting preservice teachers’ multiperspective professional vision in virtual learning environments – On the effects of modeling videos and prompts during video-based lesson analysis
citation: Janeczko, J. M., Lehmkuhl, A., Junker, R., Zucker, V., Meschede, N., & Holodynski, M. (2026). Promoting preservice teachers' multiperspective professional vision in virtual learning environments – On the effects of modeling videos and prompts during video-based lesson analysis. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10546-2
title: Teacher education programs should use video-based virtual learning environments for individualized promotion of professional vision
description: The article recommends that teacher education programs adopt video-based virtual learning environments that provide individualized learning paths, immediate feedback, and adaptive progression to promote professional vision. The VLE enables learners to progress at their own pace, with each learning unit requiring a defined level of competence before advancing. The study showed that such environments improved multiperspective professional vision compared to untreated controls.
requirements: The VLE must provide preprogrammed feedback based on expert assessments and adaptive learning paths based on preservice teachers' learning progress.
constraints: The content of the VLE must be adapted to the subject and school type, including knowledge input, classroom video selection, analysis tasks, master ratings, and feedback.
target_learners: preservice teachers in elementary science education
target_learning_goals: multiperspective professional vision of classroom management and instructional support
examples: The study's VLE consisted of five modules with increasing complexity, combining knowledge input via animated videos and quizzes with video analyses using closed and open response formats with automated feedback.
key_sources: Janeczko, J. M., Lehmkuhl, A., Junker, R., Zucker, V., Meschede, N., & Holodynski, M. (2026). Promoting preservice teachers' multiperspective professional vision in virtual learning environments – On the effects of modeling videos and prompts during video-based lesson analysis. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10546-2

article_title: Metacognition design framework to aid metacognitive skill development in university students supported by the virtual learning environment
citation: O'Neill, E. J., Fulton, C., Matthews, J., & Hensey, C. (2026). Metacognition design framework to aid metacognitive skill development in university students supported by the virtual learning environment. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10574-y
title: Use the VLE to extend metacognitive influence on student activity outside class time with realistic staff input, and re-frame educators as designers
description: The article recommends harnessing VLEs as more than repositories: "Virtual Learning Environments provide a unique, and potentially powerful, opportunity to influence student learning outside standard class time with realistic levels of staff input". The Metacognition Design Framework operationalizes this by mapping learning journeys and aligning technology via affordance analysis, providing "a practical way to re-frame educators as designers, increasing educator design capacity". Design sequences give educators a graphical, adaptable planning tool linking face-to-face and online components.
requirements: Educators create module-specific Metacognition Design Sequences from the generic blueprint
Affordance analysis aligning each learning task's requirements with technology or face-to-face options
constraints: Technology is 'the tool' and not 'the solution'; social and human dimensions of the context must also change
target_learners: university students in blended or fully online modules
examples: Guidance notes in online Appendix 1 explain planning a Learning Journey and applying the I-SEE strategies; Appendix 2 aligns technology with the strategies through affordances
key_sources: O'Neill, E. J., Fulton, C., Matthews, J., & Hensey, C. (2026). Metacognition design framework to aid metacognitive skill development in university students supported by the virtual learning environment. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10574-y

article_title: The Effectiveness of a Programme-Based Vocabulary Learning Strategies for Developing English Vocabulary for EFL Female Students at Taif University
citation: Ismaiel, N. M., & Al Asmari, A. A. (2017). The Effectiveness of a programme-based Vocabulary Learning Strategies for Developing English Vocabulary for EFL Female Students at Taif University. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 8(3), 113-125. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.3p.113
title: Vocabulary Learning Strategies Training Programme
description: A 12-week vocabulary learning strategies training programme for EFL students, based on Schmitt's (1997) VLS taxonomy, covering determination, social, memory, cognitive, and metacognitive strategies. The programme was delivered to the experimental group alongside their regular English course.
requirements: Delivered alongside a regular EFL course over 12 weeks
constraints: Studied only with Saudi female EFL students at Taif University
key_sources: Ismaiel, N. M., & Al Asmari, A. A. (2017). The Effectiveness of a programme-based Vocabulary Learning Strategies for Developing English Vocabulary for EFL Female Students at Taif University. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 8(3), 113-125. https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.3p.113

article_title: Evaluating a preclinical orthodontic training using haptic-enhanced VR simulation system: a longitudinal study.
citation: Liu Luwei, Qin Jinwei, Pan Yongchu, Wang Hua, Lu Xiaoqing, Chu Fengqing, Wang Lin, Hao Aimin, Yan Bin, Yuan Siyang. (2025). Evaluating a preclinical orthodontic training using haptic-enhanced VR simulation system: a longitudinal study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07036-7
title: Virtual orthodontic training system combining the VLNP online platform and the VSTES haptic VR simulator
description: A two-part virtual training system developed by Nanjing Medical University for preclinical orthodontic bracket bonding. The online Virtual Learning Network Platform (VLNP) lets students "undertake unlimited practice of all the procedures on the virtual learning environment in their own time", while the offline Virtual Simulation Training and Evaluation System (VSTES) provides haptic force feedback via two force-feedback devices and a 3D mouse, simulating the full bracket-bonding process with automated scoring and real-time feedback. Software copyrights are registered (online 2024SR0073414, offline 2021SR1708239).
requirements: Requires force-feedback hardware and a 3D mouse for the offline haptic section; online training requires only a computer mouse.
constraints: The article states the online VLNP supports only a two-dimensional environment inconsistent with the real clinical setting, and the offline system's micro-displacement accuracy and movement rate need improvement.
target_learning_goals: psychomotor skills of orthodontic bracket bonding, including cleaning, etching, rinsing, drying, and three-dimensional bracket positioning
examples: 26 postgraduates completed one week of online VLNP training and six weekly offline VSTES sessions, assessed by 3D laser scanning of bracket positions before and after training.
key_sources: Liu Luwei, Qin Jinwei, Pan Yongchu, Wang Hua, Lu Xiaoqing, Chu Fengqing, Wang Lin, Hao Aimin, Yan Bin, Yuan Siyang. (2025). Evaluating a preclinical orthodontic training using haptic-enhanced VR simulation system: a longitudinal study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07036-7

article_title: The virtual asthma guideline e-learning program: learning effectiveness and user satisfaction.
citation: Kang Sung-Yoon, Kim Sae-Hoon, Kwon Yong-Eun, Kim Tae-Bum, Park Hye-Kyung, Park Heung-Woo, Chang Yoon-Seok, Jee Young-Koo, Moon Hee-Bom, Min Kyung-Up, Cho Sang-Heon. (2018). The virtual asthma guideline e-learning program: learning effectiveness and user satisfaction. The Korean Journal of Internal Medicine. https://doi.org/10.3904/kjim.2017.017
title: VLCAM: a four-section e-learning program for the Korean asthma guideline
description: The Virtual Learning Center for Asthma Management (VLCAM) is a computer-based interactive e-learning program built on the Korean Asthma Management Guideline. It "consists of four sections: asthma guideline e-book, self-assessment, problem-based learning with a virtual patient, and online reference room." The virtual patient section presents complaints as text with voice narration plus photographs, radiographs, laboratory findings and auscultation sounds, and users perform history-taking, diagnosis and management decisions. The reference room supplies guideline documents, management cards, action plans, and patient handouts.
requirements: Requires computer/web access; guideline documents in the reference room are hosted at the program's associated websites
constraints: Content is limited to the Korean Asthma Management Guideline for Adults 2007
target_learning_goals: Knowledge, attitude, and practice of asthma guideline management
examples: Physicians-in-training at six tertiary hospitals used the program for 2 weeks in a questionnaire-based study
key_sources: Kang Sung-Yoon, Kim Sae-Hoon, Kwon Yong-Eun, Kim Tae-Bum, Park Hye-Kyung, Park Heung-Woo, Chang Yoon-Seok, Jee Young-Koo, Moon Hee-Bom, Min Kyung-Up, Cho Sang-Heon. (2018). The virtual asthma guideline e-learning program: learning effectiveness and user satisfaction. The Korean Journal of Internal Medicine. https://doi.org/10.3904/kjim.2017.017

citation: Sahan Bulathwela, María Pérez-Ortiz, Aldo Lipani, Emine Yilmaz and John Shawe-T aylor. (2020). Predicting Engagement in Video Lectures. https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.00592
title: Large public dataset of 4,063 video lectures with population engagement labels and cross-modal/video features
description: The article introduces a dataset built from the VideoLectures.Net OER repository for predicting context-agnostic engagement. It restricts to "lectures that has been viewed by at least 5 unique users, leading to the ﬁnal dataset having 4,063 lectures" across 21 subjects, with labels computed from 155,850 user view log events between December 8, 2016 and February 17, 2018. The dataset, code and best performing model are released publicly, including 13 cross-modal features and video-based features such as lecture duration, is chunked, lecture type, speaker speed and Silence Period Rate.
requirements: Lectures must have been viewed by at least 5 unique users to receive a population engagement label
constraints: Engagement labels are computed from English lectures and English translations of non-English lectures
Data come from peer-reviewed conference talks in one OER repository, which the authors note may limit applicability to other educational material
target_learners: online learners of open educational resources across 21 subjects
target_learning_goals: predicting and recommending engaging educational video lectures
examples: The dataset was used to train Ridge, SVR, kernelised and Random Forest regressors with 5-fold cross-validation
key_sources: Sahan Bulathwela, María Pérez-Ortiz, Aldo Lipani, Emine Yilmaz and John Shawe-T aylor. (2020). Predicting Engagement in Video Lectures. https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.00592

article_title: Virtual high voltage lab: gamified learning in a safe 3d environment
citation: Pliuhin, V., Tsegelnyk, Y., Sukhonos, M., Biletskyi, I., Plankovskyy, S., and Sakhoshko, T. (2024). Virtual High Voltage Lab: Gamified Learning in a Safe 3D Environment. O.M. Beketov National University of Urban Economy in Kharkiv.
title: VLab-HV: a photorealistic 3D virtual high-voltage laboratory built in Unreal Engine 5
description: VLab-HV is a fully immersive three-dimensional virtual laboratory replicating a real high-voltage facility, developed in Unreal Engine 5 using Lumen, Nanite, and Chaos Physics. It supports "ten curriculum -aligned experiments for undergraduate students in Power Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Electromechanics" covering discharges, polarity effects, and electrostatic barriers. Its "C++-based physics engine encapsulates complex scientific models, enabling real-time simulations of phenomena like Paschen's law, corona discharges, and partial discharges." Virtual instruments model real equipment with printed specifications (kilovoltmeters 0–100 kV, ±0.1% accuracy; oscilloscopes 100 MHz, 1 GS/s).
requirements: A system capable of running Unreal Engine 5; a "Light" version exists for low-end systems with 8 GB RAM and integrated GPUs
constraints: The supplied text reports no comparative evaluation results for the platform's learning outcomes
target_learners: second- and third-year undergraduate students in Power Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Electromechanics
electricians and professionals in HV-related industries
target_learning_goals: high-voltage engineering concepts: electrical discharges, breakdown voltage, corona and partial discharges, insulation design, safety protocols
examples: Ten curriculum-aligned experiments including electrode-configuration breakdown voltage studies under AC and DC voltage, with and without dielectric barriers (Table 1)
key_sources: Pliuhin, V., Tsegelnyk, Y., Sukhonos, M., Biletskyi, I., Plankovskyy, S., and Sakhoshko, T. (2024). Virtual High Voltage Lab: Gamified Learning in a Safe 3D Environment. O.M. Beketov National University of Urban Economy in Kharkiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20919

article_title: Virtual high voltage lab: gamified learning in a safe 3d environment
citation: Pliuhin, V., Tsegelnyk, Y., Sukhonos, M., Biletskyi, I., Plankovskyy, S., and Sakhoshko, T. (2024). Virtual High Voltage Lab: Gamified Learning in a Safe 3D Environment. O.M. Beketov National University of Urban Economy in Kharkiv.
title: Moodle API integration and Excel-compatible data logging in VLab-HV
description: VLab-HV connects to institutional learning infrastructure in two ways. "Integration with Moodle via API enables instructors to track student progress, collect performance data, and provide targeted feedback, fostering a data -driven pedagogical approach." Separately, "The platform's data logging system records experimental parameters, such as voltage, current, electrode distance, and environmental conditions, in Excel -compatible formats, supporting advanced statistical analyses like regression mode ling or Monte Carlo simulations." C++ export code (Listings 3–4) writes logged data to files for instructor and researcher use.
requirements: A Moodle instance with API access for instructor tracking; file-write access for Excel-compatible data export
constraints: The article describes the integration functionally; no evaluation of its pedagogical effect is printed in the supplied text
target_learning_goals: progress tracking, data-driven feedback, statistical analysis of experimental parameters
examples: C++ SaveArray function (Listings 3–4) exports logged experimental data to Excel-compatible files
key_sources: Pliuhin, V., Tsegelnyk, Y., Sukhonos, M., Biletskyi, I., Plankovskyy, S., and Sakhoshko, T. (2024). Virtual High Voltage Lab: Gamified Learning in a Safe 3D Environment. O.M. Beketov National University of Urban Economy in Kharkiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20919

article_title: Virtual high voltage lab: gamified learning in a safe 3d environment
citation: Pliuhin, V., Tsegelnyk, Y., Sukhonos, M., Biletskyi, I., Plankovskyy, S., and Sakhoshko, T. (2024). Virtual High Voltage Lab: Gamified Learning in a Safe 3D Environment. O.M. Beketov National University of Urban Economy in Kharkiv.
title: AI-driven virtual assistant with NLP, voice prompts, and facial tracking in VLab-HV
description: VLab-HV includes an AI assistant that guides learners through experiments. "The AI-driven virtual assistant, powered by Unreal Engine's behavior tree system and integrated with a natural language processing (NLP) module, supports voice prompts and facial tracking for an immersive user experience." It uses "a decision -making algorithm to guide users through experiments, administer real -time quizzes, and provide context -sensitive feedback." It also administers a quiz-based pre-assessment of 10 questions with a 60% passing score, incentivizing preparation through gamified rewards.
requirements: Unreal Engine behavior tree system and an integrated NLP module; quiz content aligned to the course's theoretical knowledge
constraints: The article attributes a 20% cognitive-load reduction to studies on adaptive learning systems, not to its own measured evaluation
target_learners: undergraduate engineering students using the virtual laboratory
target_learning_goals: procedural guidance through HV experiments, theoretical pre-assessment, context-sensitive feedback
examples: Quiz-based pre-assessment: 10 questions, 60% passing score, with gamified rewards for preparation
key_sources: Pliuhin, V., Tsegelnyk, Y., Sukhonos, M., Biletskyi, I., Plankovskyy, S., and Sakhoshko, T. (2024). Virtual High Voltage Lab: Gamified Learning in a Safe 3D Environment. O.M. Beketov National University of Urban Economy in Kharkiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20919

article_title: Proficiencies of military medical officers in intubating difficult airways.
citation: Lim Jonathan ZM, Chew Shi Hao, Chin Benjamin ZB, Siew Raymond CH. (2020). Proficiencies of military medical officers in intubating difficult airways. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-020-00375-2
title: Use channeled King Vision or McGrath video laryngoscopes as first-line laryngoscopes for anticipated difficult airways, especially out of hospital
description: The article recommends video laryngoscopy over direct laryngoscopy when a difficult airway is anticipated: "our study team recommends VL (KVC and MG) to be the first line laryngoscope for intubating anticipated difficult airways, especially in out-of-hospital settings." The rationale is that first attempts at difficult airways tend to be the best, since repeated attempts may cause laryngeal trauma, and the study showed KVC and MG improved success rates over DL. The recommendation is limited to the channeled King Vision and McGrath devices studied, not the non-channeled King Vision.
requirements: Devices with the studied properties: portable, battery-operated, attached screen, disposable single-use blades suited to austere environments
constraints: Supported only by manikin simulation with junior operators
Applies to KVC and MG, not to the non-channeled KVNC, which performed worse than DL
target_learners: Junior doctors and military medical officers with limited intubation experience
target_learning_goals: Emergency airway management and tracheal intubation proficiency in difficult airways
examples: 133 medical officer cadets were randomly sequenced through DL, KVC, KVNC and MG on a SimMan 3G difficult-airway trauma scenario in a 3-period, 3-treatment crossover design
key_sources: Lim Jonathan ZM, Chew Shi Hao, Chin Benjamin ZB, Siew Raymond CH. (2020). Proficiencies of military medical officers in intubating difficult airways. BMC Emergency Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12873-020-00375-2
